---
title: "Is the mean or median a better summary of a numeric variable?"
---

## Immediate answer

```{r setup-quick-mean-median, include=FALSE}
knitr::read_chunk('../examples/mean_median.R')
```

```{r quick-mean-median}
#| echo: true
#| eval: true
```

## What to change

Replace `faithful$waiting` with your **numeric measurement** column. The example records time in minutes; replace the unit with the one your dataset actually records. `mean(x,trim=.1)` computes a **10% trimmed mean** by dropping approximately 10% from each end before averaging; `median(x)` selects the middle ordered value.

## What to check

Verify numerical type and missing values. A mean is pulled toward extreme measurements; the median is less affected. Neither is always the "correct" single summary when there are clusters. A 10% trimmed mean is not the mean after deleting arbitrary outliers.


## Interpretation

An arithmetic mean adds all usable observations and divides by their number. A median marks the halfway point in ordered measurements. A **quartile** marks a quarter-position cutoff in the sample. These describe the recorded cases; population inference requires evidence about how those cases were selected.

## Retention practice (optional)

Using the built-in `airquality` dataset, find the mean, median, and 10% trimmed mean of usable `Wind` measurements. Check the original unit and decide whether a single average describes the observed distribution well.
